html:
The Tuxá are an Indigenous people of the São Francisco River in northeastern Brazil, around Rodelas in Bahia and nearby Pernambuco. Their own language is lost; they now speak Portuguese.

From the 1600s missionaries and cattle ranchers moved up the São Francisco, and the Tuxá lived in mission villages on the river islands, farming the flood plains. In the 1980s a hydroelectric dam at Itaparica flooded their island lands and old town, and the families were resettled. Their neighbours include the Pankararu and Atikum. See also Portuguese Brazil.
